props.title: Knowledge Graph
props.sub: the layer of memory — the ontology, filled with your real world

props.title: Classes become nodes; rules become edges
props.foot: The class :Report becomes the node ‘Regional Sales’; the rule :uses becomes a real edge.

props.title: Three rules that keep a graph clean instead of a hairball

cards.head: Relationships are first-class
cards.body: If you'll ever ask about a connection, make it a real edge — not a foreign key hidden inside a row.

cards.head: Node vs. property
cards.body: Something you query or connect to becomes a node. A plain attribute stays a property on one.

cards.head: Beware super-nodes
cards.body: A single node with a million edges wrecks performance — model around the hotspots deliberately.

props.foot: Good graph modeling is mostly deciding what deserves to be an edge, and what doesn't.

props.title: Property graph vs RDF triplestore — pick by the job

left.head: Property graph
rows: Fast to model, great developer velocity.
Cypher / the new ISO GQL for queries.
Best for operational apps and analytics.

right.head: RDF triplestore
rows: Pure triples with global, shareable IDs.
Best for interop, governance, shared meaning.

props.foot: Many teams do both: RDF for the meaning contract, a property graph for speed. Bridges exist.

props.title: Relationships are where relational databases hurt

left.head: SQL, many joins
rows: Queries get slow and unreadable fast.

right.head: Graph traversal
rows: A hop is just following an edge.
The query reads like the question.

props.foot: Relational is great for rows. Graphs win the moment the question is about connections.
Each silo keeps its home; the graph just adds the connective tissue between them.
Match on keys and context, collapse the duplicates — meaning stays consistent everywhere.

props.title: Every fact should say where it came from — and when

cards.head: Source on every fact
cards.body: Each node and edge records which of the six sources produced it, and when — so you can always trace a claim.

cards.head: Bitemporal history
cards.body: Keep what was true, and when you learned it. Now you can ask ‘what did the graph believe last Tuesday?’

cards.head: Confidence scores
cards.body: LLM-extracted edges carry a confidence; the shaky ones get flagged for human review, not trusted blindly.

props.foot: A graph you can't audit is a rumor mill. Provenance is what makes it evidence.

props.title: Ask a question that no single table could answer
props.caption: one traversal spans a report, its table, and yesterday's schema change
props.foot: This is a graph's superpower: multi-hop questions become a single, fast walk.

props.kicker: YOU MAY ALREADY HAVE HALF OF ONE
props.title: A data catalog is a knowledge graph in disguise

cards.head: Assets as nodes
cards.body: Tables, columns, dashboards, jobs — the things a catalog already tracks — are graph nodes.

cards.head: Lineage as edges
cards.body: ‘This report reads that table’ is exactly the edge a lineage tool already draws.

cards.head: Go further
cards.body: Add services, incidents, owners and docs, and the catalog becomes the living map.

props.foot: DataHub, OpenMetadata and Atlan are graphs under the hood — a real running start.

props.title: The best retrieval uses both meaning and structure

left.head: Vector search
rows: Great for ‘find me something about X’.

right.head: Graph traversal
rows: Great for ‘how is X connected to Y’.

props.foot: Store embeddings ON the graph nodes: retrieve by meaning, then expand along the edges.

props.kicker: WHEN IT GROWS — AND WHEN IT'S OVERKILL
props.title: Making graphs fast, fresh, and used only where they earn it

cards.head: Index & partition
cards.body: Index the properties you look up by; partition huge graphs. Azure Cosmos DB even speaks the Gremlin graph API.

cards.head: Build incrementally
cards.body: Re-ingest only what changed — logs stream, wikis update nightly. Never rebuild the whole world.

cards.head: Know the limits
cards.body: No multi-hop questions? A graph is overkill. Reach for it exactly where the connections carry the value.

props.foot: A graph is a tool, not a religion. Use it where relationships are the point.

props.note: Microsoft Research — accuracy on multi-hop enterprise questions
props.foot: Structured retrieval finds the PATH, not just similar-sounding paragraphs.
